title: Normalized closure transposes under compatible changes of left adjoints
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal P,\mathcal Q$ be categories [def-nagata-category]. Give functors $C_S:\mathcal A\to\mathcal P$, $C_T:\mathcal B\to\mathcal Q$, pairs $F_e,F'_e:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $F_p,F'_p:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$, fixed functors $E_e:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $E_p:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$, and adjunctions $F_e\dashv R$, $F'_e\dashv R$, $F_p\dashv J$, $F'_p\dashv J'$ [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Give natural isomorphisms $r_e:F_e\xrightarrow{\sim}F'_e$, $r_p:F_p\xrightarrow{\sim}F'_p$; the adjunction $F'_e\dashv R$ is transported from $F_e\dashv R$ along $r_e$. Let $t:J\xrightarrow{\sim}J'$ be the conjugate of $r_p^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Let $\mathcal A_0\subseteq\mathcal A$ be full. On $\mathcal A_0$ give natural isomorphisms $\Delta:C_TF_e\xrightarrow{\sim}F_pC_S$, $\Delta':C_TF'_e\xrightarrow{\sim}F'_pC_S$, $B:C_TE_e\xrightarrow{\sim}E_pC_S$ and natural isomorphisms $q_e:F_e\xrightarrow{\sim}E_e$, $q'_e:F'_e\xrightarrow{\sim}E_e$, $q_p:F_p\xrightarrow{\sim}E_p$, $q'_p:F'_p\xrightarrow{\sim}E_p$. Assume
$$r_{p,C_SL}\Delta_L=\Delta'_LC_T(r_{e,L}),\quad q_{p,C_SL}\Delta_L=B_LC_T(q_{e,L}),\quad q'_{p,C_SL}\Delta'_L=B_LC_T(q'_{e,L}),\quad q'_pr_p=q_p.$$
Assume $C_T$ is injective on $\operatorname{Hom}(F_eL,E_eL)$ for $L\in\mathcal A_0$. Then $q'_{e,L}r_{e,L}=q_{e,L}$. If $h:F_pC_SL\to C_TM$ and $h_0:F_eL\to M$ satisfy $h\Delta_L=C_T(h_0)$, set $h'=hr_{p,C_SL}^{-1}$ and $h'_0=h_0r_{e,L}^{-1}$. Then
$$h'\Delta'_L=C_T(h'_0),\quad \operatorname{adj}'_e(h'_0)=\operatorname{adj}_e(h_0),\quad \operatorname{adj}'_p(h')=t_{C_TM}\operatorname{adj}_p(h),\quad h'(q'_{p,C_SL})^{-1}=h q_{p,C_SL}^{-1}.$$
Fix $M\in\mathcal B$ with $H=RM\in\mathcal A_0$. Suppose isomorphisms $\gamma:C_SH\xrightarrow{\sim}JC_TM$, $\gamma':C_SH\xrightarrow{\sim}J'C_TM$ satisfy the two normalized counit equations
$$\epsilon^p_{C_TM}F_p(\gamma)\Delta_H=C_T(\epsilon^e_M),\qquad \epsilon'^p_{C_TM}F'_p(\gamma')\Delta'_H=C_T(\epsilon'^e_M).$$
Then $\gamma'=t_{C_TM}\gamma$. For any isomorphism $\rho:C_SH\xrightarrow{\sim}W$ in $\mathcal P$, the maps $\theta=\rho\gamma^{-1}$, $\theta'=\rho(\gamma')^{-1}$ satisfy $\theta't_{C_TM}=\theta$. All these comparisons respect identities and composition of successive $r_e,r_p$ obeying the displayed squares. Composition is read right to left; only the displayed Hom sets require faithfulness.

proof.text:
Fix $L\in\mathcal A_0$ and suppress component subscripts. The three comparison squares and $q'_pr_p=q_p$ give
$$B C_T(q'_e r_e)=q'_p\Delta' C_T(r_e)=q'_pr_p\Delta=q_p\Delta=B C_T(q_e).$$
Cancel the isomorphism $B_L$ and use exactly the assumed injectivity on $\operatorname{Hom}(F_eL,E_eL)$ to obtain $q'_er_e=q_e$. No faithfulness on any other Hom set is used.

proof.text:
The first square gives $r_p^{-1}\Delta'=\Delta C_T(r_e^{-1})$. Therefore
$$h'\Delta'=h r_p^{-1}\Delta'=h\Delta C_T(r_e^{-1})=C_T(h_0r_e^{-1})=C_T(h'_0).$$
By the transported Hom formula of [lem-sfb-adjunction-transport-left-iso],
$$\operatorname{adj}'_e(h'_0)=\operatorname{adj}_e(h'_0r_e)=\operatorname{adj}_e(h_0).$$
Also $q'_p r_p=q_p$ gives $(q'_p)^{-1}=r_pq_p^{-1}$, hence $h'(q'_p)^{-1}=h r_p^{-1}r_pq_p^{-1}=h q_p^{-1}$.

proof.text: Prove the transpose formula directly from the counit equation of the conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], without introducing an indexed family. Apply the injective inverse Hom bijection [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] for $F'_p\dashv J'$ to both sides of $\operatorname{adj}'_p(r_p^{-1}\gg h)=\operatorname{adj}_p(h)\gg t$. Its right side becomes $F'_p(\operatorname{adj}_p(h))\gg F'_p(t)\gg\epsilon'_p$. Replace $F'_p(t)\gg\epsilon'_p$ using Mathlib's conjugateEquiv_counit by $r_p^{-1}\gg\epsilon_p$. Naturality of $r_p^{-1}$ moves it past $F'_p(\operatorname{adj}_p(h))$, and the inverse Hom formula reduces $F_p(\operatorname{adj}_p(h))\gg\epsilon_p$ to $h$. This gives the required identity for the specified adjunctions directly.

proof.text:
Put $N=C_TM$, $h=\epsilon^p_NF_p(\gamma)$, and $h_0=\epsilon^e_M$. The first normalized counit equation is $h\Delta_H=C_T(h_0)$. Step 2 thus yields
$$h r_{p,C_SH}^{-1}\Delta'_H=C_T(\epsilon^e_M r_{e,H}^{-1}).$$
The transport formula [lem-sfb-adjunction-transport-left-iso] and the inverse Hom formula [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] imply $\epsilon'^e_M=\epsilon^e_M r_{e,RM}^{-1}$: both are the inverse transpose of $1_{RM}$ for the transported adjunction. The second normalized equation and cancellation of $\Delta'_H$ now give
$$\epsilon'^p_NF'_p(\gamma')=h r_{p,C_SH}^{-1}.$$
By the inverse Hom formula, $\operatorname{adj}_p(h)=\gamma$ and $\operatorname{adj}'_p(\epsilon'^p_NF'_p(\gamma'))=\gamma'$. Apply step 3 to conclude $\gamma'=t_N\gamma$. Here $H=RM\in\mathcal A_0$ is exactly what permits using the squares at $H$.

proof.text:
Since $t_N$ and $\gamma$ are isomorphisms, step 4 implies $(\gamma')^{-1}=\gamma^{-1}t_N^{-1}$. Thus
$$\theta't_N=\rho(\gamma')^{-1}t_N=\rho\gamma^{-1}t_N^{-1}t_N=\rho\gamma^{-1}=\theta.$$
This uses the same arbitrary $\rho:C_SH\xrightarrow{\sim}W$ on both sides.

proof.text: For successive changes write $r_e:F_e\to F'_e$, $s_e:F'_e\to F''_e$ and similarly $r_p,s_p$, with corresponding $t:J\to J'$ and $u:J'\to J''$. Substitution in the squares gives $s_pr_p\Delta=\Delta''C_T(s_er_e)$ and $q''_ps_pr_p=q_p$. Left-adjunction transport composes, since its Hom formula [lem-sfb-adjunction-transport-left-iso] gives $\operatorname{adj}''_e(a)=\operatorname{adj}'_e(a s_e)=\operatorname{adj}_e(a s_e r_e)$. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], the conjugate of $(s_pr_p)^{-1}=r_p^{-1}s_p^{-1}$ is $ut$, and the conjugate of an identity is an identity. The transported arrows satisfy $h''=h r_p^{-1}s_p^{-1}=h(s_pr_p)^{-1}$ and $h''_0=h_0(s_er_e)^{-1}$. Thus the normalized extension, square and transpose identities of steps 1–3 for the composite are precisely those obtained successively. For the normalized counit solutions step 4 gives $\gamma''=u\gamma'=ut\gamma$; step 5 gives $\theta''ut=\theta't=\theta$. With identity changes every displayed transported arrow is unchanged. This proves identity and composition for all the comparisons claimed. In Lean equality of transported adjunctions is checked on units using Adjunction.ext and ofNatIsoLeft_unit. Equality of conjugate isomorphisms is checked on their hom transformations using conjugateEquiv_comp; conjugateEquiv_id gives the identity case. Componentwise isomorphism cancellation proves the inverse formulas with the same arbitrary rho.
